mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has trended upward from -16.4% to -14.9% over four weeks, signaling gradual recovery in consumer mobility. This positive momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above the recent baseline mean of -15.9%.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 1.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days (-15.9%), or reverses to decline below -16%.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (mean 8.2% over four weeks) indicates sustained essential-goods shopping behavior. Consumers making frequent pharmacy and grocery trips exhibit higher propensity for adjacent retail-and-recreation purchases, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the two weeks following sustained GROCERY_PHARM elevation above 5%, or GROCERY_PHARM drops below 3%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains suppressed (mean -14.2% over four weeks), indicating weak commuting and public-transport-dependent retail access. This persistent transit deficit constrains RETAIL_REC recovery, preventing upward movement beyond current levels over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -12% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -12%, or TRANSIT rebounds above -10%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -18.4% to -21.3% over four weeks, signaling weakening office attendance and commuting. This deterioration in workplace activity reduces foot traffic to retail corridors and transit-adjacent shopping, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 2.9 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above -13% over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -20%, or WORKPLACES recovers above -18%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility exhibits high volatility (12.9%, -3.6%, -7.1%, 7.6%) while RETAIL_REC shows steady improvement. When PARKS and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions, it signals substitution between outdoor and indoor recreation. A positive PARKS reading (7.6% at t-0w) combined with rising RETAIL_REC indicates consumers are diversifying activity venues, sustaining retail momentum over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 5% while RETAIL_REC is above -15%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 7.6% and RETAIL_REC at -14.9% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks when PARKS is above 5%, or both PARKS and RETAIL_REC decline simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has increased from 2.3% to 4.0% over four weeks, indicating more time spent at home. Elevated home time correlates with reduced retail-and-recreation mobility as consumers substitute in-home activities for out-of-home shopping and entertainment. This residential elevation will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 3.5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased 1.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above -14% over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 3.5%, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: Weak TRANSIT (-14.4% at t-0w) combined with suppressed WORKPLACES (-21.3% at t-0w) indicates policy-driven mobility restrictions or voluntary avoidance of public spaces. This dual suppression constrains the consumer base accessible to retail venues. Recovery in RETAIL_REC will only occur if both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rebound simultaneously, signaling policy relaxation. Over the next four weeks, without such dual recovery, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -13% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -14.4% and WORKPLACES at -21.3% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1.5 percentage points over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -13%, or either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rebounds above -10%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM elevated at 7.4% (t-0w) reflects seasonal holiday shopping preparation and essential-goods stockpiling behavior typical of mid-November. This seasonal surge in grocery mobility will extend into retail-and-recreation venues as consumers engage in holiday shopping, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks as the holiday season intensifies.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 6% during November-December period
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 7.4% at t-0w in mid-November
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 6%, or GROCERY_PHARM drops below 4% before December.
